steps.title: AO5 & AO6
steps.body: Paragraphing demonstrates your ability to organise ideas effectively. Examiners look for well-structured writing with clear paragraph breaks and coherent organisation.

steps.title: Purpose
steps.body: A strong topic sentence sets up your paragraph, guides the reader, and makes your argument clear from the start.

steps.title: Tip
steps.body: Use long paragraphs to develop ideas and short paragraphs for impact. A one-sentence paragraph can be powerful in narrative writing.

steps.title: Paragraphing Exam Strategy
steps.body: Good paragraphing shows the examiner you can organise your ideas — it's essential for both AO5 (structure) and AO6 (cohesion). Before writing: Plan your paragraph structure. For an argument, know what each paragraph will argue. For a narrative, know the TiP ToP shifts. For an article, know which point each paragraph makes. During writing: Use topic sentences to open paragraphs. Link each paragraph to the previous one using connectives or referencing. Vary paragraph length — a short, one-sentence paragraph can create dramatic impact. Mark allocation: AO5 (24 marks) rewards well-organised writing with clear paragraph structure. AO6 (16 marks) rewards cohesion — how well your paragraphs link together to form a coherent whole. What examiners look for: Clear paragraph breaks at logical points.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: What does TiP ToP stand for? | Write a topic sentence for a paragraph about a writer's use of rhetorical questions. | When should you start a new paragraph in dialogue?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Time, Place, Topic, Person - the four main reasons to start a new paragraph | Example: "The writer employs rhetorical questions to engage the reader and prompt reflection." | Start a new paragraph for each new speaker

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Plan your paragraphs before you start writing Use TiP ToP to know when to start new paragraphs Start each paragraph with a clear topic sentence Use connectives to link paragraphs smoothly Vary paragraph length for effect Check dialogue has proper paragraph breaks Leave time to review structure at the end
